headline: Phillies shut out by Rays despite Sánchez's 10 strikeouts
recap: The Phillies fell to the Tampa Bay Rays 2-0 at Citizens Bank Park on Friday night, their third straight loss. Tampa Bay scored in the top of the first when Jonny DeLuca's sharp single to right drove in Junior Caminero, then added an insurance run in the top of the second on a Nick Fortes solo home run to left. Cristopher Sánchez pitched well in defeat, working seven innings and allowing both runs on five hits with 10 strikeouts and one walk, but took the loss to fall to 18-7. Freddy Peralta got the win for Tampa Bay, striking out four over 5.1 scoreless innings, and Bryan Baker closed it out for his 41st save. The Phillies managed only four hits and were shut out, with no player recording an extra-base hit.

Philadelphia is 87-73, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves, and has dropped three in a row. The Phillies currently hold the National League's third and final Wild Card spot.

Philadelphia continues its series against the Rays on Saturday at Citizens Bank Park, with first pitch scheduled for 7:15 PM ET. Tampa Bay's Griffin Jax is set to start; the Phillies had not yet announced a starter. Philadelphia is a slight favorite at -105 on the moneyline, with Tampa Bay at -114.
